entities.summary:
The First Battle of Gaza took place on March 26, 1917, during the Middle Eastern theater of World War I. This pivotal event in the campaign against the Ottoman Empire marked a significant turning point in the war, as the British forces, led by General Edmund Allenby, successfully captured the city of Gaza, securing a crucial victory for the Allies.

The First Battle of Gaza had far-reaching consequences, as it paved the way for the eventual capture of Jerusalem by the British in December 1917. This, in turn, had a profound impact on the region, as it led to the redrawing of the Middle East's borders and the eventual establishment of the State of Israel in 1948.

As Lord Allenby himself noted, 'The capture of Gaza was a turning point in the war, marking the beginning of the end of the Ottoman Empire.' His words would prove prophetic, as the fall of the Ottoman Empire would have a lasting impact on the modern Middle East, shaping the region's politics, cultures, and economies for generations to come.

The legacy of the First Battle of Gaza can still be felt today, as the city remains a strategic hub of regional politics and a testament to the enduring power of military conquest in shaping the course of human history.
